title: The Book of Amos Timeline
sub: The LORD Roars From Zion · Let Justice Roll Like a River
desc: A herdsman from Tekoa pronounces judgment on nation after nation until it lands squarely on Israel itself, confronting economic exploitation and empty religious ritual before closing in a promise to rebuild David's fallen dynasty.

eras.label: Era One · Amos 1
eras.name: The LORD Roars From Zion — Judgment on the Nations Surrounding Israel
eras.dates: A herdsman from Tekoa opens with a repeated formula of judgment, working through the nations surrounding Israel one by one before the oracle turns, unexpectedly, toward Israel itself

events.title: Three Crimes, Even Four: Judgment on Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom, and Ammon
events.detail: Using a repeated 'three crimes, even four' formula, Amos pronounces fiery judgment on Israel's neighbors one after another (Damascus, Gaza, Tyre, Edom, Ammon) building audience sympathy before the target shifts closer to home.

verses.text: “The LORD [Yahweh] comes roaring out of Zion; from Jerusalem he comes bellowing! The shepherds' pastures wilt; the summit of Carmel withers.”

eras.label: Era Two · Amos 2
eras.name: Judgment on Moab, Judah, and Israel Itself
eras.dates: The judgment formula finally lands on Judah and then Israel, turning what sounded like foreign-policy commentary into a direct indictment of the audience itself

events.title: They Sold the Innocent for Silver: the Formula Finally Lands on Israel
events.detail: After Moab and Judah, the same judgment formula finally strikes Israel, indicted for selling the poor into debt-slavery and profaning worship itself with cynical religious hypocrisy: despite being the very people the LORD rescued from Egypt.

verses.text: “They sold the innocent for silver, the needy for a pair of sandals. They trample on the dirt-covered heads of the poor.”

eras.label: Era Three · Amos 3
eras.name: Does a Lion Roar Without Cause? — the LORD Reveals His Plan to the Prophets
eras.dates: A series of cause-and-effect questions establishes why judgment is certain, and why Amos himself can't help but speak it

events.title: The Sovereign LORD Does Nothing Without Revealing His Plan to the Prophets
events.detail: A rapid series of cause-and-effect questions (does a lion roar without prey, does an alarm sound without cause) builds to the principle that the LORD never acts without first revealing his plan through the prophets, explaining why Amos cannot stay silent.

verses.text: “Certainly the Sovereign LORD [Adonai Yahweh] does nothing without first revealing his plan to his servants the prophets.”

eras.label: Era Four · Amos 4
eras.name: Cows of Bashan — Yet You Did Not Return to Me
eras.dates: Wealthy women who oppress the poor are addressed directly, followed by a refrain listing disaster after disaster that failed to produce genuine repentance

events.title: You Cows of Bashan: You Oppress the Poor
events.detail: Wealthy women of Samaria who demand more drink while crushing the needy are compared to well-fed cattle, mocked alongside the empty, performative worship they love to display at Bethel and Gilgal.

verses.text: “Listen to this message, you cows of Bashan who live on Mount Samaria! You oppress the poor; you crush the needy.”

events.title: Still You Did Not Come Back to Me: Prepare to Meet Your God
events.detail: A five-fold refrain lists famine, drought, blight, plague, and destruction, each disaster meant to prompt repentance and each ending in the same devastating line: still you did not come back to me.

verses.text: “Prepare to meet your God, Israel!… The LORD [Yahweh] God [Elohim] of Heaven's Armies is his name!”

eras.label: Era Five · Amos 5
eras.name: Seek the LORD and Live — Let Justice Roll Like a River
eras.dates: A funeral song for a nation not yet dead builds toward one of the most quoted calls for justice in the Bible, aimed squarely at empty religious ritual

events.title: Seek the LORD So You Can Live
events.detail: Amos sings a funeral dirge for a still-living Israel, urging the nation to seek the LORD rather than the compromised worship sites of Bethel and Gilgal, and to promote justice rather than merely mourn once disaster finally arrives.

events.title: Let Justice Roll Like a River: I Despise Your Festivals
events.detail: The LORD declares he despises Israel's religious festivals and noisy worship music, demanding instead that justice flow like an unending stream: a verse later echoed directly by Martin Luther King Jr.

verses.text: “Justice must flow like torrents of water, righteous actions like a stream that never dries up.”

eras.label: Era Six · Amos 6
eras.name: Woe to Those at Ease in Zion
eras.dates: The wealthy elite who lounge on ivory couches unconcerned about national ruin are told they will be the very first to go into exile

events.title: Woe to Those Who Live in Ease: Not Concerned Over the Ruin of Joseph
events.detail: The nation's comfortable upper class, lounging on ivory-decorated couches and drinking the best wine, are condemned for their total indifference to the coming ruin, promised they will lead the procession into exile.

verses.text: “They lie around on beds decorated with ivory and sprawl out on their couches. They eat lambs from the flock and calves from the middle of the pen.”

eras.label: Era Seven · Amos 7
eras.name: Three Visions — Locusts, Fire, and a Plumb Line — Amos Confronts Amaziah
eras.dates: Three escalating visions of judgment culminate in a direct confrontation between the prophet and a hostile royal priest

events.title: Locusts, Fire, and a Plumb Line
events.detail: Three visions escalate in severity: locusts and fire that Amos successfully intercedes against, then an uncompromising plumb line measuring Israel crooked, which the LORD will no longer overlook.

verses.text: “I am about to place tin among my people Israel. I will no longer overlook their sin.”

events.title: I Was Not a Prophet by Profession: Amaziah Confronts Amos
events.detail: The priest Amaziah orders Amos to leave Bethel and prophesy for pay back in Judah; Amos answers that he was never a professional prophet at all, just a herdsman the LORD took directly from the flock to send to Israel.

verses.text: “I was not a prophet by profession… I was a herdsman… the LORD [Yahweh] took me from tending flocks and gave me this commission.”

eras.label: Era Eight · Amos 8
eras.name: A Basket of Summer Fruit — a Famine of Hearing the Words of the LORD
eras.dates: A wordplay vision on ripeness and ending leads into one of the most haunting judgments in the prophets, not a famine of food, but of God's own word

events.title: A Basket of Summer Fruit: the End Has Come
events.detail: A Hebrew wordplay on 'summer fruit' and 'the end' announces that Israel is fully ripe for judgment, indicted specifically for merchants eager for the Sabbath to end so they can resume cheating the poor with rigged scales.

verses.text: “The end has come for my people Israel! I will no longer overlook their sins.”

events.title: A Famine of Hearing the Words of the LORD
events.detail: The coming judgment is described not merely as bread and water scarcity but as a total famine of divine revelation itself: people wandering everywhere searching for a word from the LORD and finding none.

verses.text: “I will send a famine through the land—not a shortage of food or water but an end to divine revelation… the words of the LORD [Yahweh].”

eras.label: Era Nine · Amos 9
eras.name: None Can Escape — I Will Rebuild the Fallen Hut of David
eras.dates: The book's harshest vision of inescapable judgment gives way, in its final verses, to one of the Old Testament's most hopeful promises of restoration

events.title: None Will Be Able to Escape: Yet I Will Not Completely Destroy Jacob
events.detail: In vivid, inescapable imagery (digging to the netherworld, climbing to heaven, hiding at the bottom of the sea) the LORD promises none of the sinful nation can outrun judgment, though he also promises not to utterly destroy the family of Jacob.

verses.text: “Even if they could dig down into the netherworld, my hand would pull them up from there. Even if they could climb up to heaven, I would drag them down from there.”

events.title: I Will Rebuild the Fallen Hut of David
events.detail: The book that opened with the LORD roaring in judgment closes in restoration: David's collapsed dynasty rebuilt, exiles returned, vineyards replanted, and a promise that Israel will never again be uprooted from its land.

verses.text: “In that day I will rebuild the collapsing hut of David. I will seal its gaps, repair its ruins, and restore it to what it was like in days gone by.”
